ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 - ENGL 301 - Intro to Critical Theory - Hina Nazar - This course offers a broad-based introduction to some of the most important schools of criticism and theory that have shaped the academic study of literature since the 1940s. These include foundational schools such as the New Criticism, Marxism, feminism, postcolonial studies, queer theory, and critical race studies, as well as recent developments such as the digital humanities, ecocriticism, and posthumanism. Key questions our readings raise include: Why should we study literature in an academic context? Is interdisciplinarity the future of literary studies? What kind of weight should we ascribe to form, as opposed to context, in approaching literary works? Is literature an agent of social and political change? How is agency figured in literary texts? In literary and critical theory? While one aim of the course is to introduce you to key theoretical perspectives informing literary and cultural studies, another, equally important, one, is to encourage you to reflect on your own status as a critical reader of and writer about literature. As such, we will keep literature firmly in our sights as we proceed through the semester’s readings.**Non-majors who wish to take ENGL 301 may email englishadvising@illinois.edu to request an override.**
